_readme: Which BDB defs stand as a lemma's short gloss, for the words where the
entry's first sense misleads a reader. Used by buildGlossIndex in
scripts/lib/oshb.mjs, which writes public/data/morphhb/glosses.json.
A pin chooses, it never writes. Every string in `gloss` and `stems` must be
a def the BDB entry itself carries, and the build fails on one that is not,
so the wording on the page stays the lexicon's (Mitch, Oct 2026).
gloss:  replaces the head gloss, in the order given.
stems:  stem name (as morph-parse.ts renders it) -> the sense to list first
for that stem. The entry's own senses follow it, minus repeats.
why:    what the unpinned gloss says, and why that misleads.
tbesh:  what STEPBible's TBESH (Translators Brief lexicon of Extended Strongs
for Hebrew, CC BY 4.0, Tyndale House / STEPBible.org) gives as this
lemma's main gloss, or null if it has none. Required on every pin.
Before adding a pin (Mitch, Oct 2026):
1. pnpm check:pins <lemma>   shows BDB's defs (the only words a pin may use)
and TBESH's glosses for the word.
2. Choose BDB defs; copy TBESH's first gloss into `tbesh`.
3. Where the pin and TBESH differ, say so in `why`.
4. pnpm check:pins            must pass.
TBESH is a witness, not a source: its wording never reaches the app.
Only pin a word a reader meets often. The long tail reads BDB as written.

85.why: The entry is Abram's, so the head reads 'Abram, Abraham'.

341.why: OSHB's lemma is the noun אֹיֵב; BDB files it under the verb, 'be hostile to'.

413.why: The head is BDB's description, 'motion to or direction towards'.

430.why: Sense 1.a is the rare 'rulers, judges'; 2,598 occurrences are almost all God.

571.why: The head stops at 'firmness, faithfulness'; 'truth' is several senses down. TBESH leads with 'truth', where this pin leads with 'faithfulness'.

854.why: The second item, 'proximity', is the root's sense, not the preposition's.

977.why: BDB's Qal senses are headed by kind — 'divine choice', 'man's choice' — not by meaning.

996.why: The head is the noun sense, 'interval, space between'.

1288.why: BDB's Piel senses describe who blesses whom ('bless God', 'God blesses'), not what the stem means.

1961.why: BDB leads with 'fall out', the archaic English for 'happen'.

2706.why: The head opens with BDB's description, 'something prescribed'.

3426.why: The head is the noun sense, 'being, substance'; the word nearly always means 'there is'. TBESH: 'there'. BDB's entry has no 'there'; 'is, are' is the nearest it carries.

3966.why: The head is the noun sense, 'muchness, force'; the word is nearly always the adverb. TBESH: 'much'. BDB has 'muchness', not 'much'; 'very' is the adverb it carries.

4994.why: BDB splits 'I pray' into two defs, so the head reads 'I, pray'. TBESH: 'please'. Not in BDB's entry; 'pray' is the same courtesy in BDB's English.

5048.why: The head opens with the noun sense, 'what is conspicuous'. TBESH: 'before'. Not in BDB's entry; 'in front of' is the nearest it carries.

5750.why: The head opens with the root's sense, 'a going round, continuance'.

5769.why: 'Antiquity' second suggests the past; the word mostly looks forward. TBESH: 'forever: enduring'. BDB's entry in this file is three defs and none is 'for ever'; this is the nearest. A known gap of the BDB-only rule.

6153.why: The head opens with 'set', from BDB's note on sunset.

6726.why: The head opens with the transliteration 'Ṣiyyôn'.

6944.why: 'Apartness' alone, first, reads as a spatial word. TBESH: 'holiness'. BDB's entry in this file is only 'apartness, sacredness'. A known gap of the BDB-only rule.

7650.why: The only Qal sense is a cited phrase, 'those sworn with oaths'.

7965.why: BDB lists 'peace' fourth, after 'completeness, soundness, welfare'.

8199.why: The Qal opens with 'act as law-giver, judge', which is too long for the gloss line and leaves 'act as law-giver' on its own.

8478.why: The head opens with the noun sense, 'the under part'.

5921a.why: The entry opens on its rare noun sense, 'height'; the preposition is sense II.

310a.why: The head is the noun sense, 'the hinder or following part'.

3820a.why: BDB lists 'heart' fourth, after 'inner man, mind, will'.

2896a.why: BDB leads with 'pleasant, agreeable'. TBESH agrees on the words but leads with 'pleasant', BDB's own order. 'Good' first is a judgement TBESH does not corroborate.

5387a.why: The head opens with the root's sense, 'one lifted up'. TBESH: 'leader'. Not in BDB's entry; 'a chief prince' is the nearest it carries.

7235a.why: The head's defs are a phrase split across a comma, so it reads 'be, become, much'. TBESH: 'to multiply'. Not in BDB's entry; 'become many' is the nearest it carries.
